claims.claim_text: W-1 stated that the subject possessed a single firearm, a small handgun.
At approximately 0022 hours, the Tactical Response Group (TRG) was activated and assumed responsibility for the incident.
Beginning at approximately 0308 hours, Officer Vega, the primary negotiator, began making PA announcements encouraging the subject to exit the residence peacefully.
At approximately 0314 hours and again at 0322 hours, the subject briefly emerged onto the rear patio of the residence, shouted at officers, and returned inside each time.
At approximately 0341 hours, the subject came out onto the front porch and pointed what appeared to be a handgun directly at officers using both hands in a shooting stance.
At approximately 0350 hours, in response to a recorded surrender request from W-1, the subject emerged holding a short-barreled rifle with a standard 30-round magazine.
The subject exited the front door holding the same rifle in his left hand.
The subject raised the rifle to shoulder level and pointed it directly at the marked K9 patrol vehicle parked in front of the residence where several officers were positioned.
The subject fell forward onto the porch in a prone position.
The subject was observed lying face-down with no weapon in his hands.
Officer Kapoor deployed two 40 mm Less Lethal rounds as a precaution but the subject showed no response.
Officer Diaz subsequently deployed the K9, which made contact with the subject and pulled him from the porch onto the sidewalk.
A subsequent search of the residence recovered one firearm: a .38 caliber revolver, Smith and Wesson, found on the porch near the front door. No rifle was recovered from the residence.
Anaheim Fire Department paramedics arrived at approximately 0404 hours; the subject was pronounced deceased at approximately 0411 hours.
The situation was classified as a Negotiator Driven Incident under Penal Code section 1370 due to information that the subject had previously been found mentally incompetent.
